mechanics.title: Max Send: destination-side, shared stock cap
mechanics.summary: Max Send is stored on the destination building per product and shared by every origin shipping that product there. It caps the destination's stock including incoming reservations (in-flight and queued deliveries). It is not a per-trip amount and not a per-route quota. 0 (shown as infinity in the UI) means unlimited.
mechanics.formula: headroom = max(max_send - (stored + incoming_reserved), 0); max_send = 0 => unlimited

evidence.note: cap on the destination's stock, stored on the destination, shared, 0 = unlimited

mechanics.title: Max Send range and UI stepping
mechanics.summary: Setting Max Send writes the destination's storage cap, clamped to the destination's per-product slot count. Stepping with the UI arrows wraps: below 0 jumps to the slot count, above the slot count wraps to 0 (unlimited).

mechanics.formula: available = max(origin_stock - min_keep, 0); keep_all => route never dispatches

mechanics.title: Per-trip dispatch amount
aliases: how much does a truck carry
mechanics.summary: The amount a route requests per dispatch is computed, never stored: the minimum of vehicle capacity, origin stock above Min Keep, and destination free space under the Max Send headroom, with extra caps from active contracts and world events. With 'fill vehicles' set, nothing is sent until a full load is possible.
mechanics.formula: amount = min(cap, max(origin_stock - min_keep, 0), min(free_space, max_send_headroom)); wait_for_full and amount < cap => 0

mechanics.title: Dispatch cost (per vehicle dispatch)
mechanics.summary: Each vehicle dispatch costs a formula of route distance, the difficulty dispatch parameter and an actor modifier. Manual routes with own trucks use ManualDestinationDispatchCost; depots and terminals use their own, more expensive formulas. The cost is paid once per vehicle at dispatch, so a half-empty vehicle costs as much as a full one.
mechanics.formula: ManualDestinationDispatchCost = (250 + distance * 10) * difficulty * actor; TruckDepot = (350 + distance * 15) * difficulty * actor; TrainTerminal = (2250 + distance * 25) * difficulty * actor

mechanics.title: Shop demand
mechanics.summary: Each shop's demand per product is recomputed at every city consumption tick from city population, the producing recipe's time and output, a tier value and the shop's demand modifier, then multiplied by the product's demand modifier and capped. mechanics.summary: Difficulty 'prices' is an additive price offset; 'upkeep' multiplies building upkeep; 'dispatch' is the difficulty argument of dispatch-cost formulas; 'loan' sets the starter loan. The 'demand' and 'balance' fields are not read anywhere in code.

evidence.note: demand and balance: no reads found in Assembly-CSharp

mechanics.caveats: AI difficulty presets override only dispatch, prices and upkeep.
